For ready reference, the aforesaid order is reproduced herein under:
"Heard Mr. Anand Kumar Srivastava, the learned counsel for applicant and the learned A.G.A. for State.
Perused the record.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant Devendra Tiwari seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 80 of 2023, under Sections 304-B, 498-A IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Khanpur, District Ghazipur during the pendency of trial.
Record shows that marriage of Ashutosh Tiwari, son of applicant was solemnized with Jyoti sister of first informant on 3.12.2017.

However, after expiry of period of five years and six months from the date of marriage of son of applicant, an unfortunate incident occurred on 11.6.2023, in which the daughter in law of the applicant Jyoti died as she consumed some poisonous substance.
It is the case of applicant that information regarding aforesaid occurrence was given by the mother in law of deceased to the brother of deceased.

It is on the aforesaid information that the brother of the deceased/first informant came to the marital home of the deceased and thereafter took the victim to the hospital where she was declared brought dead.

On the information given by Vivek Tiwari, the brother of deceased first informant,
Inquest (Panchayatnama) of the body of deceased was conducted.
In the opinion of witness of inquest (panch witness), no opinion could be expressed with regard to the nature of death of deceased and cause of death of deceased.
Thereafter, post mortem of body of deceased was conducted.

The Doctor who conducted autopsy of the body of deceased opined that cause of death of deceased cannot be ascertained, therefore,
viscera was preserved.
Autopsy surgeon, did not find any external ante-mortem injury on the body of deceased.

After aforementioned proceedings had been undertaken, a belated F.I.R. dated 13.6.2023 was lodged by first informant, which was registered as Case Crime No. 80 of 2023, under Sections 304-B, 498-A IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station- Khanpur, District Ghazipur.

In the aforesaid F.I.R. four persons namely, Ashutosh Tiwari, Devendra Tiwari, Bindu Devi and Piyush Tiwari, have been nominated as Ashutosh Tiwari vs State Of U.P. on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124411325/

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant contends that though the applicant is father-in-law of deceased, named and charge-sheeted accused, yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
The deceased was a short tempered lady.
She has taken the extreme step of terminating her liefe by consuming some poisonous substance.
As per F.S.L. report dated 1.8.2023, organo, chloro insecticide was found in the body parts of the deceased sent for chemical examination.
The bonafide of the applicant is explicit from the fact that no external anti-mortem injury was found on the body of deceased.

Referring to the F.I.R., the learned counsel for applicant contends that the only allegation made in the F.I.R. is that additional demand of dowry was made, and since the same was not fulfilled, physical cruelty was committed upon deceased.

However,
the said allegations are not only false and concocted but also vague and bald as they are devoid of material particulars.
Reference in this regard is made to the judgement of Supreme Court in Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others Vs. State of Bihar and Others, (2022) 6 SCC 599.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Others Vs. State of Bihar and Others, (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the basis of above, it is urged by learned counsel for applicant that since allegations made in the F.I.R. regarding demand of dowry and commission of cruelty upon deceased on account of non fulfilment of additional demand of dowry are devoid of material particulars, therefore, the same are liable to be ignored by this Court, at this stage.
Even otherwise, applicant cannot be said to be the benificiary of alleged demand of dowry.
Son of the applicant is already languishing in jail.
Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in jail since 8.8.2023.
As such, he has undergone more than three months of incarceration.

The police report in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted against applicant, as such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by prosecution against applicants stands crystalized.
However, upto this stage no such incriminating circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
It is thus urged that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. and the learned counsel for first informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
They submit that since applicant is a named as well as charge sheeted accused, therefore he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
The death of deceased has occurred at her marital home before expiry of a period of seven years from the date of marriage.
As such, the death of deceased is a dowry death.
Applicant is an inmate of the house and father-in-law of the deceased.
As such, the burden is upon the applicant to not only explain the manner of occurrence under Section 106 but also his innocence under section 113 of the Evidence Act.
However, the applicant has miserably failed to discharge the said burden upto this stage.

As such, no sympathy be shown by this Court in favour of Ashutosh Tiwari vs State Of U.P. on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124411325/

(i) THE APPLICANT SHALL FILE AN UNDERTAKING TO THE EFFECT THAT HE/SHE SHALL NOT SEEK ANY ADJOURNMENT ON THE DATE FIXED FOR EVIDENCE WHEN THE WITNESSES ARE PRESENT IN COURT.
